sync.title: Organisation server
sync.lead: Optional: a shared store of the organisation's cases — hand-over between investigators, roles, audit log. Without signing in the app works fully offline and sends nothing anywhere.
sync.privacy: Cases are sent to the server only when you press “Send”, and only to the address you enter here. The server address and deployment guide come from your organisation's administrator.
sync.registerHint: Once, for the organisation's first administrator. If registration on the server is closed, ask the administrator to create a user for you.
sync.name: Name
sync.conflict: The server has version {v} — someone changed the case after you. Overwrite it with your copy?
sync.replaceLocal: The case “{title}” already exists in this browser. Replace it with the server copy?
sync.none: No cases on the server yet.
sync.resetPrompt: Temporary password for the user (at least 8 characters). Tell them in person; they will change it in the Server section.
sync.addUserHint: Tell the temporary password in person. Roles: administrator — users and case deletion; investigator — reads and writes cases; reader — read only.
sync.act.case.create: case sent for the first time
sync.autoPushed: Case completed and sent to the server
sync.orgExportHint: Backup: one JSON file with all the organisation's cases (attachments included). Keep it as an official record.
sync.orgImportHint: Uploading a backup adds missing cases and updates those that are newer in the file; older and foreign cases are skipped.
sync.orgImportConfirm: Upload {n} cases from the backup of “{org}” to the server? Cases whose version is not newer than the server's will be skipped.
sync.orgImported: Restore: added {imported}, updated {updated}, skipped {skipped}, with errors {errors}

sync.err.registration-closed: Registration on this server is closed.
sync.err.password: Password must be at least 8 characters.
sync.err.bundle: The server rejected the case package.
sync.err.too-large: The case is too large to send (reduce attachments).
sync.err.not-found: No such case on the server.
sync.err.version-conflict: The server has a newer version of the case — get it, or overwrite with “Send”.
sync.err.id-mismatch: The case identifier does not match the package.
sync.err.json: The server could not parse the request.
sync.err.internal: Internal server error — try again later.

cases.title: Worked examples from the QRG
cases.lead: The three SOAM charts published in the EUROCONTROL guide (pp. 47–49). Loading replaces a previously loaded copy.
occ.typeHint: Definitions of accident and incident — ICAO Annex 13 (QRG, p. 6).
occ.severityHint: The EUROCONTROL severity scheme (QRG, p. 7) applies to incidents; not required for accidents. SOAM is recommended for levels A, B and C.
occ.advice.required: An accident is always investigated (ICAO Annex 13; QRG, p. 7).
occ.advice.recommended: Severity {severity}: use of SOAM is highly desirable (QRG, p. 7).
occ.advice.costBenefit: Severity {severity}: decide by a cost/benefit analysis (QRG, p. 7). Record in the justification:
occ.advice.unknown: Assess the severity — the recommendation to investigate depends on it (QRG, p. 7).
occ.advice.cb1: what safety lessons the investigation could yield;
occ.advice.cb2: what resources (people, time, data) it would need.
occ.advice.conflict: The decision “do not investigate” departs from the methodology — give a justification.
occ.advice.label: Methodology recommendation
occ.advice.pirate: Hypothetical PIRATe scenario: severity and the decision to investigate are not assessed; the analysis follows the same SOAM process (QRG, p. 55).
occ.modeHint: PIRATe (QRG, pp. 54–56): a group of subject matter experts “designs our next accident” and analyses it with the same SOAM process — facts, sorting, chart, actions. The mode is chosen at creation.
occ.pirateGuide: How to run a PIRATe exercise
pirate.reason.forecast: Forecast: “our next accident” from knowledge of local hazards
pirate.reason.change: Change: new procedure, technology, equipment or facility
pirate.reason.repetitive: Repetitive events: AIRPROX, runway incursions, technical failures, etc.
occ.participantsPlaceholder: Positions and units of participants (no names), date and format of the session
occ.titlePlaceholderPirate: e.g. Scenario: runway incursion while working two frequencies
occ.scenarioOutcomePlaceholder: One item per line: which accident is being designed, possible consequences
report.kickerPirate: Proactive risk assessment using PIRATe (based on SOAM)
occ.outcomePlaceholder: One item per line: what happened, consequences, damage
anon.title: Anonymised copy
anon.hint: For handing the case to another organisation, for training material or for AI (stage 5). Texts are passed through replacements, attachments are not included, codes and links are kept. Check the preview: the automatic rules do not know names — add them to the replacement table.
anon.dictionary: Replacement table (one per line: original → replacement; no replacement — [REDACTED])
anon.dictPlaceholder:
J. Smith → CONTROLLER-1
Dushanbe → AERODROME-A

anon.autoRules: Replaced automatically: e-mail → [EMAIL], phone numbers → [PHONE], aircraft registrations (EY-, UK-, RA-…) → [AIRCRAFT], flight callsigns (three letters and a number) → [FLIGHT].

about.title: About the method
about.intro: SOAM (Systemic Occurrence Analysis Methodology) is EUROCONTROL's methodology for the systemic analysis of aviation safety occurrences. The app guides the investigator through the SOAM steps and uses the terms, codes and check questions of the Quick Reference Guide (QRG).
about.rights: QRG material © EUROCONTROL. Used with attribution, non-commercially, without altering the English wording.
about.step.register: Register the occurrence and assess severity (A–E)
about.step.shelo: Gather facts with the SHEL/O model
about.step.sort: Sort facts: contribution test and check questions
about.step.chart: SOAM Chart: barriers, human involvement, contextual conditions, organisational factors
about.step.actions: Safety actions (every barrier and every OSF addressed by at least one action; SMARTER)
about.translation: The Russian translation is machine-made and under review. Tajik is in progress.
occ.statusHint: “Completed” opens from the “Actions” status when the readiness summary on the QA tab is green.
chart.howToLink: Links: click a node, then a node in the neighbouring column — the link appears; click the same pair again to remove it. Barrier → outcome works the same way.
chart.selected: Node selected — choose the second one.
chart.unconfirmed: Classifications without a confirmed check question: {n} (red border). Confirm them on the Sorting tab.
chart.sameLevel: A link is possible only between different columns
actions.addressesHint: An action addresses barriers and organisational factors, not people and their actions (QRG, p. 51).
actions.noTargets: No barriers or OSFs yet — classify the facts first.
actions.responsiblePlaceholder: Unit or position, not a person's name
actions.coverageOk: All {n} barriers and OSFs are addressed by actions.
actions.rule4: SOAM rule: every absent or failed barrier and every organisational factor must be addressed by at least one action (QRG, p. 50). A barrier without a stated state is treated as needing an action.
actions.err.addresses: Specify which barriers or OSFs the action addresses

qa.hint: Tick items as they are completed; the note says where to find the evidence.
qa.ready: All conditions are met — the case can be completed.
qa.notReady: The case cannot be completed while there is a ✗.

report.finalNote: QA completed — this is the final report.
report.draftNote: QA checklist {done} of {total} — the report prints as a draft (SOAM rule: report after QA).

qa.lessonsHint: QRG, QA item 12: key lessons from the occurrence are identified and widely disseminated. One lesson per line.
